fields.reasoning: No owner words; read the change set intent, internal/api/daemon.go and internal/adapter/claudecode. The intent asks for per-window use from the adapter's token records, a reserve setting, a skip reason in status/health/inbox, and resuming on reset. The disk-low guard (rhiza.daemon.minFree) is the existing precedent for a resource hold. It stops picks, resumes, queued work and plans, but leaves live runs alone. Copying its scope keeps the daemon consistent, and it protects the reserve, which exists for the owner's own use. Claude Code publishes no token limits, so the limit must be either configured or learned. The adapter already detects usage-limit hits (UsageLimit and PaneUsageLimit) with a reset time, so the use seen at a hit gives a calibration without any setup. No known limit means no hold, so the governor fails open instead of blocking work on a guess. Cache reads dominate the raw totals and are weighted far below fresh tokens, so counting them would swamp the signal. The account is shared, so the owner's interactive sessions eat the same window and must count. Averaging recent runs per live and next run projects whether the next pick fits. Extrapolating to the window's end would hold early in every window.
fields.statement: (1) When: at each poll the governor checks two windows, the 5-hour session window and the 7-day weekly window. A window starts at the first token record after the previous window ended, or at the reset time a usage-limit message gave. Each window has a limit: the daemon setting for that window (tokens) if set, else the window use at the last usage-limit hit in that kind of window. A run driver that sees a hit records its time and reset time where the daemon reads it at each poll. The hit's kind comes from its reset time: a reset 5 hours or less after the hit is the session window, a later one the weekly window. A hit with no reset time teaches nothing. A window with no known limit never holds. The reserve is a daemon setting, a percentage of the limit, default 20%. The daemon holds a new pick when the window's use so far, plus the mean tokens of the last 10 finished runs for each live run and for the one it would start, exceeds the limit minus the reserve. With no finished runs to average, only the use so far counts. (2) Tokens: input, output and cache-creation tokens count, for the session and its helpers; cache-read tokens do not. They come from every Claude Code transcript on the machine, the owner's own sessions included, since they share the account. Only records timestamped inside the window count, each message once (deduplicated by message id, as TokenUse already does). (3) Scope: a hold works like the disk-low guard. It stops everything the daemon would launch: picks, its resumes of interrupted runs, queued starts and continues, and plan requests. Each held change set shows as a skip with reason usage-reserve, giving the window, use, limit and reset time in its detail, in daemon status, health and the inbox. It never interrupts live runs, and it does not stop runs the owner starts directly outside the daemon. It clears on its own at the first poll after the window resets.

fields.acceptance: A test in internal/adapter/claudecode builds a fake config dir with transcripts in two project dirs, a message repeated across content-block lines, a helper's lines, cache-read tokens and records before and after the span, and gets the exact expected records, each with its timestamp and token count, in time order; no file outside the fake config dir is read
fields.statement: An adapter reports the token records between two times across every one of its transcripts on the machine, each with its timestamp and its counted tokens; the Claude Code adapter reads sessions and their helpers under <config>/projects, each message once by id, counting input, output and cache-creation tokens and never cache reads, and only records timestamped inside the span

fields.acceptance: Unit tests in a pure internal package, over timestamped token records as usage-window-tokens returns them and limit resets with fixed times, cover a first window, a record just after a window ended starting the next one, a gap with no records, and a usage-limit reset moving the start, for both window kinds
fields.statement: The governor tracks a 5-hour session window and a 7-day weekly window, each starting at the first token record after the previous window of its kind ended, or at the reset time a usage-limit message gave, and knows each window's start, reset and use so far

fields.acceptance: A test in internal/api's daemon tests with a fake adapter: a run driver's limit hit with a reset 3 hours out is recorded and becomes the session window's learned limit in the daemon's state, one with a reset 4 days out becomes the weekly one, one with no reset time teaches nothing; a later poll holds on a learned limit with no setting, a set rhiza.daemon.usage.session wins over it, and a window with no setting and no hit never holds
fields.statement: When a run driver sees its session stop at a usage limit, it records the hit's time and reset time in the git common dir's rhiza state, which the daemon reads at each poll. The hit's window kind comes from its reset time: a reset 5 hours or less after the hit is the session window, a later one the weekly window, and a hit with no reset time teaches nothing. The daemon saves that window's use at the hit as the learned limit for its kind and uses it whenever the setting for that window is unset; a window with neither limit never holds
